newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair offers Heathrow ground handling.
newsitem.headline: Swissair offers Heathrow ground handling.

text.p: Swissport International AG, a subsidiary of Swissair AG, said on Friday it would begin offering ground handling services at London's Heathrow Airport as part of its strategy of expanding worldwide.

Swissport, the former Swissair Ground Services, said it had also acquired 40 percent of the share capital of Airport Services Muenchen GmbH (ASM), the largest independent provider of passenger services at Munich airport.
The remaining 60 percent of ASM will be retained by Flughafen Muenchen GmbH, the airport's authority, Swissport said in a statement.
The moves by Swissport are part of Swissair's group strategy of spinning-off many activities into independent units, which then can offer their services in the market place.
A Swissport spokesman said the company was working on expanding in other airports, but declined to specify which.
"We are working on other projects and are trying to expand worldwide," he said.
Swissport also has a 50-50 joint venture with an Israeli company at Tel Aviv's airport, where its customers include British Airways BA and Air Canada.

Swissport will begin its operations at Heathrow on January 14, initially providing handling services for the 16 daily flights at the airport from Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Crossair AG, Swissair's regional carrier.
The spokesman said Swissport would also offer its services to other airlines at Heathrow.
"We are a service provider and want to win customers," he said, adding, "Swissair is just one of our customers."
At Heathrow Swissport will employ a total of 80. Sixty will be newly-hired and 20 will be absorbed from Swissair's ground services in London.
In Munich, ASM's customers include Swissair, AUA, Sabena, Alitalia, Iberia and USAir.
AUA will be giving up its own passenger handling unit in Munich and all its staff will be taken over by ASM.
